title: Causal AI Architect Toolchain and Platform Boundaries
summary: Recommended tools and architectural boundaries for a production causal decision-intelligence platform.

verification.notes: Reference architecture and tool-selection guidance. It is framework knowledge, not personal production proof.

claims: Causal discovery should propose candidate structures while DoWhy or DoWhy-GCM handles identification, estimation, refutation, and counterfactual analysis.
Neo4j should store versioned causal graph structures and provenance, while the causal engine remains a separate statistical computation boundary.
The semantic knowledge graph, causal model, supporting evidence, and model versions should remain connected but not collapsed into one undifferentiated graph.

causal_claims.subject: Causal Discovery
assumptions: Data, domain constraints, and discovery assumptions are explicitly recorded.

causal_claims.subject: Causal Inference Engine
assumptions: A causal claim has an identifiable estimand, declared assumptions, and retained refutation results.

causal_claims.subject: Neo4j Operational Graph
assumptions: Statistical evidence remains linked as first-class records rather than being reduced to an edge label.
